text: The Univalence Axiom of HoTT, $\mathrm{IsEquiv}(e)\simeq\mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal{U}}(A,B)$, is captured by which slogan?
choices: Every proposition is decidable (excluded middle holds)
explanation: Univalence says an equivalence $A\simeq B$ is the same as an identification $A=B$ in the universe: 'isomorphic types are identical.' Excluded middle and computability are separate matters (Univalence is in fact non-constructive as an axiom), and 'every type is a set' contradicts HoTT, whose higher types carry nontrivial homotopy.
